EO-01.mapping_to_concept: The concept builds outputs for policy-relevant ecosystem assessment, nature protection and restoration planning, and biodiversity trend prediction. C19 names these activities verbatim, carried by P11 policy-reporting needs assessment and P10 occurrence-data facility. C07 and C17 supply predictive biodiversity trend modelling scaled from case sites to European coverage via P12. C14 shapes outputs to named reporting instruments so a competent authority can use them. The mechanism is explicit and non-contradicted.
EO-01.tier3_evidence_ref: project_summary.json C19, C07, C17, C14; concept_note.md 'The chain, from genome to space' and 'Coordination the topic requires'

EO-02.mapping_to_concept: The concept strengthens capacity of researchers, practitioners and decision-makers and integrates data across sensors from omics to satellite. C20 uses the outcome's capacity phrase verbatim, delivered through P05 user network, P11 stakeholder work and P06 protocol transfer. C02 supplies the three omics layers 'omics-based data (genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic)' verbatim via P01 and P09. C01 integrates multisensory data and C16 addresses knowledge gaps. Mechanism present and consistent.
EO-02.tier3_evidence_ref: project_summary.json C20, C02, C01, C16; concept_note.md 'The chain, from genome to space' and 'Reaching agriculture'

EO-03.mapping_to_concept: The concept reworks in-situ datasets into training and validation resources for machine learning and AI, supporting habitat classification, ecosystem mapping and trend prediction. C06 uses 'training and validation resources' verbatim, with P03 archive and a P01 leakage-safe split protocol. C07 uses 'habitat classification, ecosystem mapping and biodiversity trend prediction' verbatim via P12 deep-learning classification. Mechanism explicit and non-contradicted.
EO-03.tier3_evidence_ref: project_summary.json C06, C07; concept_note.md 'Training and validation data'

SR-01.coverage_description: The concept builds one multisensory integration system harmonising omics, in-situ and remote-sensing data (C01) and delivers predictive modelling at case, regional and European scales (C17). Harmonisation workflows carry provenance (C09).

SR-02.coverage_description: The concept delivers capabilities across terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms on one gradient (C04), a knowledge-gap analysis (C16) and predictive analytics with AI (C07). Coverage of the three realms is complete.

SR-02.notes: Partial: the concept flags thin geography (K2/F5, ten of twelve partners in three country slots) and single-partner dependency for each aquatic realm (K1/F4). The 'Member States and Associated Countries' spread is met under Assumed at six slots but is a stated weakness, not a scope gap. Non-blocking.

strategic_differentiation: One pressure gradient carries all three ecosystem realms as a single causal chain. Farmland drains into the freshwater ecotones that receive its runoff, which drain to the coastal waters downstream. A harmonisation decision taken in farmland is therefore tested twice more, in realms that did not design it. This makes integration 'across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems' evidence rather than assertion, where competing consortia assemble three unrelated sites. Two further differentiators reinforce the position: a leakage-safe validation protocol (P01) that keeps site, season and treatment in one fold, and an existing multi-country agricultural user network (P05) that carries indicators into farm-management tools. The concept also states its own weaknesses plainly, since half the consortium is Assumed and the geography is thin (K1, K2, K3).
